title: The pointers that teach the old 64-hex triage still name `ticfac finding` everywhere
description:
sg5 replaced the everyday triage path, but every surface that TELLS somebody how to triage still teaches the old one: the `ticfac findings` listing prints `ticfac finding <epic> <64-hex> --promote-as ...`, the run's own findingLeftNote (reconcile/absorb.go) tells workers the same, and the close-out's refusal message names it too. A person or agent following those pointers will type 64-hex keys and create ticks by hand — exactly the friction A3 exists to remove — even though `ticfac triage <epic>` now settles everything by short prefix. The wording lives in reconcile and the findings listing, with tests asserting the old strings, so the change is its own tick rather than part of sg5.

ticfac run epic-2jn created this tick by absorbing the finding 08af2962fdabb3d49d5ad594bc797cc607065f63142e1c8555567f6e6df762e9 (reported by run-epic-2jn/tick-sg5/attempt-4): the finding was judged against the epic's definition of done and gates the done, naming no single item (the fallback names every item at risk in its reason). The decision record — item id, verdict, observed or predicted, confidence — is .ticfac/runs/epic-2jn/absorptions/08af2962fdabb3d49d5ad594bc797cc607065f63142e1c8555567f6e6df762e9.json on the run branch.
